Arzanda was the name of a wealthy woman from Tlemcen who became a prominent figure during the Marinid period. She was known for her patronage of poets and scholars, and her salon was a gathering place for intellectuals and artists.

historical_references.context: Arzanda is mentioned as a fortress and a major trading center in the eastern desert of Egypt during the Mamluk period. It was situated near the Red Sea and was an important stopover for caravans traveling between Egypt and Yemen.
